title: Exponential witness bounds for three-dimensional VASS
formal: Do there exist constants \(C,d\in\mathbb N\), with \(C,d\ge1\), such that every reachable instance \(I=(V,s,t)\) of a three-dimensional vector addition system with states has a legal run from \(s\) to \(t\) of length at most \[2^{C(L(I)+1)^d}?\] Here \(L(I)\) is the binary description size defined below, including the finite control graph, all transition updates, and both configurations. The constants must be independent of the instance. The target is the length of an actual sequence of transitions, not the size of a compressed representation of that sequence.

source_formulation.text: For binary three-dimensional vector addition systems with states, does every reachable source–target pair admit a run of at most exponential length in the input description?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase; corrected VAS/VASS model from the source

why: Exact reachability in counter systems is decidable, but the length of the necessary witness can be vastly larger than the finite description. Dimension three is the first unresolved step beyond the exponential-witness theorem for binary two-counter systems. A positive result would yield a PSPACE upper bound for three-dimensional reachability and expose a strong structural limit on how much counter behavior finite control can force.
status_note: Source-open in CONCUR 2022, §3. The published ICALP 2025 theorem gives triply-exponential witnesses, and the 16 July 2026 preprint claims doubly-exponential witnesses; neither establishes or refutes the single-exponential bound. The August 2026 PSPACE result is for stateless VAS. Bounded later-work checking on 16 September 2026 found no matching resolution. Preprint proofs were not independently verified.

importance.reason: A central low-dimensional reachability barrier, stronger than a complexity-class upper bound and directly tied to the jump from two counters to three. Recent elementary and claimed EXPSPACE bounds still leave its single-exponential witness question unresolved.

sentences: A three-dimensional vector addition system with states combines a finite control graph with three nonnegative integer counters.
The question asks whether every reachable pair of configurations has an actual run whose length is singly exponential in the binary input size.
The same exponent bound must work for all inputs, including unbounded control graphs and arbitrary binary counter values.
Published triply-exponential and subsequently claimed doubly-exponential witness bounds leave this stronger target unresolved.
A resolution would clarify the structural and algorithmic change between exact reachability with two counters and with three.

definitions: Write \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\). A three-dimensional VASS is \(V=(Q,T)\), where \(Q=\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\) for an input integer \(q\ge1\), and \(T\) is a finite explicitly listed set of transitions \((p,a,r)\in Q\times\mathbb Z^3\times Q\). A configuration is \((p,x)\in Q\times\mathbb N^3\). The transition \((p,a,r)\) sends \((p,x)\) to \((r,x+a)\) exactly when all three coordinates of \(x+a\) are nonnegative. Counters have no fixed upper bound and no extra zero tests. Input configurations \(s=(p_s,x_s)\) and \(t=(p_t,x_t)\) must be matched exactly, in both state and counter values. A legal run of length \(h\) is a sequence of \(h\) enabled transitions whose consecutive configurations all have nonnegative counters; \(h=0\) is allowed when \(s=t\). Reachable means that at least one finite such run exists. For a completely specified size measure let \(\ell(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil\) for \(z\in\mathbb Z\), and define \[L(I)=q+|T|+\ell(p_s)+\ell(p_t)+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(\ell((x_s)_j)+\ell((x_t)_j)\bigr)+\sum_{(p,a,r)\in T}\left(\ell(p)+\ell(r)+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\ell(a_j)\right).\] This counts an explicit state list and signed binary numerical data; separators change it by at most a constant factor. It is polynomially equivalent to ordinary explicit binary encodings. Exactly three counters are fixed, but the number of states and transitions and all numerical magnitudes are unrestricted. The question is a uniform combinatorial bound; it requests no randomized guarantee, average over inputs, approximate target, or construction-time bound.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed uniform single-exponential bound. An affirmative proof must supply some fixed \(C,d\ge1\) and prove a sufficiently short actual run for every reachable instance. A refutation must prove \[\forall C,d\ge1\ \exists I\text{ reachable},\quad\text{every run from }s\text{ to }t\text{ has length }>2^{C(L(I)+1)^d}.\] One long instance only refutes a particular proposed bound. A decision procedure or succinct witness representation alone is insufficient unless its proof establishes the required bound on actual run length.

context_blocks.text: A transition adds a fixed integer vector, but it is enabled only if no counter becomes negative. The finite control graph determines which additions can follow which. Reaching a configuration with larger counters is not enough: the target includes exact counter values and a specified control state.

The source paragraph is explicitly about binary 3-VASS. The imported title abbreviated this as VAS, which would ordinarily remove the control states and change the fixed-dimensional problem. The revised title restores the model actually used by the source; it does not substitute the stateless variant.

For binary two-dimensional VASS, reachability is PSPACE-complete and every reachable pair has an exponentially bounded witness. The source asks whether this actual-run guarantee survives with three counters. It presents this as a witness-length question alongside, rather than identical to, the broader question of exact decision complexity.

The ICALP 2025 theorem provides the first elementary bound for three-dimensional VASS: reachable configurations have a run of at most triply-exponential length, yielding a doubly-exponential-space algorithm. This substantially improves the older non-elementary upper bounds but permits witnesses far larger than the single exponential asked for here.

The July 2026 preprint claims an EXPSPACE algorithm and a doubly-exponential bound on the shortest run. Its parameterized bound uses the number of strongly connected components and a numerical size convention, with the stated conclusion covering binary encoding as well. Even if all arguments are accepted, this remains a weaker upper bound than the present target.

The August 2026 preprint settles PSPACE-completeness for stateless three-dimensional VAS. A VAS lacks the arbitrary control graph allowed here; encoding that graph can require extra counters. Consequently the fixed-dimension result cannot be imported as a solution to this three-counter VASS question.
